title_en: Chinese Humor (14/20): Caught Napping by the Boss
note_en: 正 + verb (often with 着) shows an action in progress at a given moment, like the English "was ...ing": 他正做着一个美梦 "he was in the middle of a sweet dream." The next clause then brings in the interruption, here with 就在这时 "just then" and 突然 "suddenly": 一阵咳嗽声突然在耳边响起. Chinese verbs don't change form for tense, so 正…着 does the job of the English past progressive.
